lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - A Look and write

details: Look and write serves as a review of the unit’s vocabulary. Students identify the numbered food items in the picture and write them on the list to consolidate spelling.
Look for correct identification of the food items from the scene and accurate spelling of the six target vocabulary words.
“Our fridge is empty. It’s time for a trip to the big supermarket! Can you help me write a shopping list?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - B. Listen and choose

details: Listen and choose assesses students’ listening comprehension of the unit's vocabulary.
Look for focused listening and the ability to distinguish between the two options, demonstrated by accurately circling the correct letter.
“Okay shoppers, I need your expert ears to help me! I'm not sure what we need. Can you listen carefully and choose the right picture for me?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - A Find, colour, and write

details: Find, colour, and write serves as a creative review of the unit's vocabulary culminating in spelling practice.
Look for correct identification and colouring of the food items, accurate spelling of the target words and neat bookwork.
“Ok - here’s everything in our baskets. Can you check what we have, so we know what we still need to look for?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.32 - Speaking Presentation Our Fridges

details: Our Fridges is a speaking task that synthesizes the unit's vocabulary and grammar. Students use the language in a personalized, communicative context through pair work and a final presentation.
Look for confident interaction during pair work, successful information exchange (correct stickers in the friend's fridge) and a clear, audible presentation to the class.
“Time to unpack our shopping now. Let’s fill up our fridges. We have enough food for the week!”
